notes: This source/test traceability contract covers the bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Publish Object Class Attributes service in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable development profile. The declaration transition adds the supplied available attributes to the invoking federate's ordinary publication state. A focused filesystem process-restart companion now proves that publication state rehydrates with the typed object-class declaration ledger in a fresh registry; this is bounded state-image evidence, not complete publication, ownership, or routing conformance. Its focused production-filesystem regression also adds the successful-void service-report boundary: an undefined object class appends nothing, while an accepted publication appends type-36 ObjectClassHandle and type-1 AttributeHandleSet arguments before any separately queued declaration advisories or ownership-assumption work. The Requirements Lab currently assigns the §5.2 service-level candidate on its coalesced source page to clause-5.2.4; RL-078 records that ownership mismatch while the service/test descriptions retain the direct §5.2 source context. Whole-class publication removal, complete ownership/discovery behavior, advisory delivery matrices, MOM interaction delivery, timestamped behavior, remaining save/restore application ledgers, DDM, remote transport, catalog evidence, validation, and conformance remain outside this slice.
